newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh refugees begin repatriation from India.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh refugees begin repatriation from India.

text.p: Tribal refugees, who fled an insurgency in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, began returning home on Friday from camps in India's Tripura state, witnesses said.
Bangladeshi officials said the first 15 families reached Bangladesh after crossing a wooden bridge over the Feni border river following a ceremony marking the formal repatriation.
The officials said 278 refugees from 64 families were due to return later on Friday. About 7,000 refugees are expected to cross back into Bangladesh by April 7, they said.

The ceremony at a border crossing point marking Friday's refugee departure was attended by Tripura Deputy Chief Minister Baddya Nath Majumdar and Bangladesh's Abul Hasanat Abdullah, parliamentary chief whip of the Ruling Awami League.
The rebels began an insurgency in the 14,200 sq-km (5,500 sq-mile) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma in 1973 to demand political autonomy, which the government has rejected.
Officials say more than 8,000 civilians, rebels and soldiers have been killed in the fighting, which has forced nearly 50,000 tribals to flee across the border.
Some 6,000 refugees were repatriated in 1994, but the process was stopped without official explanation.
